statement: Amortization trade: moving computation from per-pair optimization into shared or per-style state lowers marginal cost by orders of magnitude; every audited within-paper comparison against per-pair or per-scene optimization reports a residual gap on the paper's own objective; comparisons against less-shared learned states usually do (CIN, AdaIN) but not always (StyleCrafter).
Zero-shot coverage is distributional: performance on unseen styles depends on proximity to and size of the training style distribution, not on the arbitrary-reference interface.
The per-content term is not monotonically eliminated: inversion-based diffusion transfer reintroduces per-content (and per-reference) computation that can dominate per-pair cost.

Every acquired style state carries a compatibility domain (style set, base-checkpoint family, scene); positive transfer evidence is confined to the same base family or to warm starts, and no audited paper tests cross-family portability.
Composition interference arises where acquired states share a binding subspace; it is asymmetric across factors and avoided only by explicit separation or low-dimensional statistic interpolation.
Cross-paper cost and quality orderings are not identified: the same method's runtime and rank change with implementation and with the metric's alignment to each method's objective.
Interventions that reduce entanglement relocate cost into acquisition (paired data, staged fitting, human selection) or into per-sample inference (inversion, guidance).
The reported reference-similarity proxies do not separately identify removal of unwanted reference semantics and reduced intended style strength in the coded sample.

Leakage has at least three intervenable sources -- representation granularity, binding locus and acquisition objective; binding interventions are documented in all three non-objective carriers, acquisition interventions in parameter and condition carriers, representation interventions only in condition carriers of the audited set.
For a fixed representation and binding, leakage and dilution are opposite ends of a strength/weight axis; only frontier comparisons at matched operating points are informative.
Causal attributions of leakage conflict across papers (training objective versus representation versus routing) and are not resolved by any audited intervention.
'Leakage' names distinct phenomena (reference-to-output semantics, content-to-output style, sibling-to-sibling, iterated target erosion); its definition depends on a declared style scope.
Style factors (colour, texture, layout) are bound through different mechanisms and are entangled both in outputs and in the metrics used to score content preservation.

Each coupling mechanism constrains a specific relation (visible flow trajectories, input-video correspondences, frozen shared geometry, a learned temporal prior), and evidence for it is confined to that relation.

Reported consistency scores depend on their correspondence system; selected comparisons favor static, blurred or weakly stylized outputs. Individual source observations are retained in the evidence register.
Selected comparisons show that improved consistency scores can coincide with weaker style fidelity; one recorded counterexample prevents a universal ordering.
Occlusion/reappearance, long horizons, geometry change and joint time-view consistency are untested or only qualitatively shown in the audited set.

Shared 3D scene representations do not uniformly outperform 2D video methods on reported metrics: they lead on short-range warped error but not consistently on long-range or reference-fidelity metrics.
